body:
### Summary

When a project depends on another project through a `path` or `git` source, uv also applies that dependency's own `[tool.uv.sources]`, including index pins. I couldn't find this in the docs, and it changes which build of a package the consuming project gets without any configuration on its side.

### Reproduction (uv 0.13.7)

`lib/pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "lib"
version = "0.1.0"
dependencies = ["torch"]

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = { index = "pytorch-cpu" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cpu"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
```

`app/pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "app"
version = "0.1.0"
dependencies = ["lib"]

[tool.uv.sources]
lib = { path = "../lib" }
```

`uv lock` in `app/` resolves `torch` from `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` (`2.15.0+cpu`), although `app` configures no index.

If `app` pins `torch` itself:

```toml
dependencies = ["lib", "torch"]

[tool.uv.sources]
lib = { path = "../lib" }
torch = { index = "pytorch-cu128" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu128"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128"
```

`uv lock` fails:

```
error: Failed to resolve dependencies for package `app==0.1.0`
  cause: Requirements contain conflicting indexes for package `torch` in all marker environments:
         - https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
         - https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
```

The same happens with `lib` as a `git` source. `--no-sources` resolves, but it also drops `app`'s own sources. `--no-sources-package lib` doesn't help either: it drops `app`'s own source for `lib`, so `lib` is resolved from PyPI instead of `../lib`.

### Question

Is this intended? It's reasonable for a path/git dependency to bring its sources along, but the first case is surprising: the consuming project silently gets a CPU build of torch because of a library's index pin.

If it is intended, I'd be happy to send a docs PR. Two places seem to fit:

- [Dependency sources](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/dependencies/#dependency-sources): a note that `tool.uv.sources` of path and git dependencies are applied too, and that conflicting index pins fail the resolution (`--no-sources` turns off all sources, including the project's own).
- [Pinning a package to an index](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/indexes/#pinning-a-package-to-an-index): a note that a pin travels to projects that depend on this one through a path or git source, so libraries may want to leave the torch index to their consumers.

If it isn't intended, I can add a test next to `lock_multiple_sources_index_overlapping_extras` that covers this case, and help with the change once you've decided how it should behave.

### Context

I ran into this when a library installed via `git` pinned `torch` to `cu128` and the application moved to `cu132`. The fix was a new tag of the library with the new index, but the coupling wasn't obvious from the docs.

### Platform

Linux x86_64

### Version

uv 0.13.7 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

3.14.10
title: Index from a path/git dependency's `tool.uv.sources` is used for the dependent project's packages
